title: Vázquez: neither charity nor faith is needed for a morally good work, only some help of grace
source_text: XXII. Concedit igitur ille nec charitatem quam Spiritus Sanctus in fidelium corda diffundit, nec ipsam fidem necessariam esse, ad hoc ut aliquis bene operetur, & legi morali atque naturali veram exhibeat obedientiam; sed ab homine non tantum in peccato jacente, verum etiam adhuc infideli, posse opus aliquod moraliter bonum procedere. Hoc solum negat hominem peccatorem, & omni gratiae divinae auxilio destitutum, posse bene agere, & secundum virtutem & honestatem naturalem.
pass_a_gloss: XXII. He grants therefore that neither the charity which the Holy Spirit pours into the hearts of the faithful, nor faith itself is necessary, for this that someone work well, and show true obedience to the moral and natural law; but that from a man not only lying in sin, but also still an unbeliever, some morally good work can proceed. This only he denies, that a sinful man, and destitute of every help of divine grace, can act well, even according to natural virtue and honesty.
pass_b_english: So he grants that neither the charity the Holy Spirit pours into the hearts of believers nor faith itself is needed for someone to act well and give true obedience to the moral and natural law. A morally good work can come from a man who is not only lying in sin but is still an unbeliever.
The one thing he denies is that a sinner, without any help of divine grace at all, can act well, even by the standard of natural virtue and honesty.

lemmas.latin: quam Spiritus Sanctus in fidelium corda diffundit
lemmas.gloss: which the Holy Spirit pours into the hearts of the faithful
destitute of every help of divine grace

choices.why: Grace given for a particular act, distinguished from God's general concurrence with all causes; 'help' keeps the scholastic auxilium.
